text: What was disputed was one blocking finding: round 3's C1, that `tests/test_hermetic.py`'s `test_both_of_the_suites_entry_points_are_hermetic` pinned one hermetic guard and not both. It is upheld, because I reproduced it rather than reasoning about it: with `hermetic.strip_git_config(os.environ)` deleted from `tests/test_00_home.py:31`, the test was `OK` while the mode that twin exists for — `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_00_home.py`, which loads the module top-level and never runs `tests/__init__.py` — was `FAILED (failures=1)` on `'core.hookspath' unexpectedly found`. A test whose comment claims "neither twin can be left behind again" while staying green with a twin broken is worse than no test, so the exact edit was a third child run of that discover mode in the same loop; it is committed at `02bc263` and the test now goes red when *either* guard is removed (verified both ways). Round 3's I1 was non-blocking but factually true on inspection — `GhHost` appears nowhere in the tree and `squash_subject` runs before `host.merge`, not after — so it is closed too at `4c6d162`, docstring only. Everything else is overruled and does not return in any later round. Round 2's I2 (the hermeticity fix belongs on its own card) is overruled as a blocker: the code is correct and this branch's gate cannot run without it, so the carve-out is a record action, not a branch change, and it is a NEEDS OPERATOR line above. Round 3's I4 and I8 (`tests/test_dry_run.py:76` asserting byte-equality over `asf/harvest/harvest.py:746`'s `{time.monotonic() - started:.0f}`, and `tools/run_tests.py` silently returning a smaller denominator under load) are overruled as against this branch — I confirmed the branch touches none of those three paths, and I saw the same flake twice and then a clean `OK` on the identical head. Round 3's I5 is an environment defect, not a branch defect. Round 3's I2, I3, I6 and I7 are overruled as grounds for a further round: I verified I7's anchors myself (`("spec", "plan")` does remain literal at `asf/evidence/evidence.py:502` and `:513`, and at `asf/harvest/lane.py:264` and `:619`), and they are a refactor of rows the card's *Expected* never names, on a branch already three rounds deep. What now holds is the card's contract, checked against the checkout and not against a review: both halves of *Expected* are implemented, and the *Acceptance* clause is `tests/test_doc_lane_landing.py:245` clause for clause — `("Active", "plan-approved")` at `:251`, `["New", "New"]` at `:253`, `rows.PLAN_CODE` per minted Task at `:259`. What changes because of it is that the review loop is closed at round 3 and the branch is landable, and that the card's empty footprint — the thing that let an unrelated hermeticity defect land here with nobody able to call it out of scope — is corrected in the `writes:` line below.

The hold was "the Gate commands are green" failing on six modules, repeated three times because no round had confirmed independently — rather than by cross-reference to another card's review — that this red exists on a clean trunk. It does: an origin/main worktree with none of B-0115's changes fails the same six modules with the same git-identity/hooksPath sandbox artifacts, unrelated to asf/scheduler.py or tests/test_scheduler.py. Round 2's verdict of approved (clean C-list, every plan Step matched to the diff, both named tests present and green) stands on its own merits and is not reopened. The gate-red hold on this item is overruled and does not return in a later round; B-0115 lands as-is.

What was disputed was whether fix/B-0114 is the cause of the three gate holds that stalled it, after four review rounds ended in approval — and, secondarily, six findings round 4 left open. The gate is the fact, and it is green: at the head before my edits the full suite ran 2808 tests across 92 modules OK, and the hermetic env -i step returned the same denominator and rc=0, so no red attributable to this branch exists to hold it. The reds that produced the holds are in modules the branch never touches — `git diff origin/main...HEAD` over `tests/test_dry_run.py`, `asf/harvest/harvest.py`, `tools/run_tests.py` and `asf/tick` is empty — and both are trunk defects: `asf/harvest/harvest.py:797` formats `{time.monotonic() - started:.0f}` into a line `tests/test_dry_run.py:76` requires byte-identical across two consecutive dry runs, which rounds to different seconds under load, and `tools/run_tests.py` reports the survivors when a pooled module process dies, giving a smaller denominator with no module named. Round 3's own origin/main baseline had test_dry_run red at the trunk. The three gate holds are therefore overruled as not this branch's, and they do not return; the branch lands as it stands. Of round 4's open findings I upheld I1, I2 and I4 and made the edits in 093180a: the --subject retry now logs the degrade instead of leaving a non-conforming trunk subject to be inferred, strips the flag by position rather than by value, and no longer fires on --rebase, which never adds it; the twin test spawns sys.executable at both sites so the hermeticity guard tests the interpreter actually running the suite. I overruled I3 — the `flag provided but not defined` alternative in SUBJECT_UNKNOWN_RE is unreachable but inert, because `_rejects_subject` (asf/harvest/lane.py:1304) also requires the literal `--subject` that Go's single-dashed form never prints, and the reviewer's proposed relaxation to `'subject' in err` would widen a retry that drops the subject, which is the precise failure this card exists to prevent. I overruled I6 — DOC_LANE_KINDS already binds the two sides this card created, the writer `squash_subject` and the reader `lane_kind`, which is what round 1's I5 asked for; the remaining literal `('spec', 'plan')` sites are a pre-existing refactor across four modules B-0114 never entered, and pulling them into a branch with no review round after it buys nothing this card needs. What changes: the card's footprint is recorded below, since `writes: (none declared)` is why scope could never be argued in any round; the two trunk flakes need their own items, and the gate's own invocations need an operator allowlist entry, both below.

What was disputed was never the code — round 3 already resolved both regressions rounds 1 and 2 found (`asf/groom/inbox.py`'s `_UNREAD_HEADER_KEYS` registry correctly drops `after:` whether or not a further confirmed header follows it, and `INBOX_KV_RE` matches keep advancing `body_start` regardless of position, so a header-shaped body line is never mistaken for a header and a real header is never mistaken for body) and was approved with a fully green gate. The STALEMATE fired because the branch was held a third time with `kind='gate'` (`asf/feeder/rows.py:368`'s `held {rounds} times ({kind})` reads back as `held 3 times (gate)`) — a harvest-time product-gate refusal *after* the content review had already approved, not a fourth content defect. Rounds 1 and 2's own reviews independently recorded the same host at load average 27-50 causing `tools/run_tests.py --shards 4` to be killed or time out before completing (`docs/reviews/1-b-0111.md` I3, `docs/reviews/2-b-0111.md`'s Gate row); round 3 only went green once load dropped to 5-9. `asf.harvest.harvest.product_gate` kills a gate past `gate_timeout_s` (default 600s, B-0072) and that refusal is handed back through `send_back`/`hold_with_correction` exactly like a real red, consuming a round — so a host-contention timeout and a genuine defect are indistinguishable to the round counter, and this item paid for the former as if it were the latter. I re-ran every gate command myself on this exact head just now, at load average 3-11: `check_generic.sh` clean, `check_conventions.sh` clean (replicated — its real invocation is sandbox-blocked in this session too), and the full suite green in 311s (2881 tests, OK, 93 modules). The gate hold is overruled — checked against `docs/reviews/1-b-0111.md` and `2-b-0111.md`'s own load-average evidence and against a fresh green run on this head; it does not come back in a later round. The only change made: `git rm .run_tests_gate.log`, the zero-byte stray file I2 flagged unresolved across all three rounds — harmless, but there is no round after this one to carry it forward in. The branch is ready to land as `8856796`.

Disputed: the STALEMATE → ADJUDICATE hold ("held 3 times (gate): adjudicate, not another correction") and round 1-4's carried I1 ("no plan and no spec for an S2 bug"). Both overruled. The gate hold: I checked the branch's actual lineage against `docs/reviews/1-4-b-0111.md` and the diff itself — rounds 1 and 2 each carried a genuinely gate-breaking head (round 1: an unrecognized header line dropped real headers after it; round 2's own fix for that introduced a fresh leak, a trailing `after:` line bleeding into the description), each closed by the next round's fix, not by wishful correction. The current head is unchanged since round 3's approval (`git diff d54eeed..HEAD -- asf/groom/inbox.py tests/test_inbox_shape.py` is empty) — round 3 ran the full declared gate to completion green (`tools/run_tests.py --shards 4`: 2834 tests OK), round 4 ran it again green (2884 tests OK), and I independently re-ran the module suite green a third time. There is no open C finding on the branch and nothing left in the code for a fourth correction session to find — exactly the "another correction will not converge" case adjudication exists for. The I1 dispute: `asf/feeder/rows.py:303` names a Bug's `## Fix` as its own plan — only Feature cards route through `docs/specs/`/`docs/plans/` (`CARD → SPEC`, `asf/feeder/rows.py:505-509`). The "acceptance tests byte-identical to the plan's" row failing every round is a checklist row that does not apply to Bug cards, not a real gap; it was correctly never treated as blocking (verdict stayed "approved" through it). What changes: the hold is lifted, the branch lands as reviewed with no further session; the card's footprint, never declared through 4 rounds, is set explicitly below so a future footprint gate has a real fence instead of none.
